forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Uttlesford expects to use reserves from 2026/27 as funding falls
news_drafts.lead: Uttlesford achieved a £0.854m underspend in 2025/26 without drawing on reserves, but the council now expects to use its reserves from 2026/27 onwards to cover projected deficits caused by reduced government funding following the Fair Funding Review. The council holds sufficient reserves to cover these deficits and is pursuing efficiency savings through its Blueprint 2.0 programme, targeting £900,000 in 2026/27 and £2.5m by 2030/31. However, the Audit and Standards Committee heard that 33 audit recommendations now remain overdue, including one critical priority item. Housing has been a persistent area of concern, with the audit identifying control weaknesses in an £8.6m maintenance contract, including undocumented payment discrepancies, and unresolved recommendations on debt recovery and project management that date back over a year.

findings.headline: Uttlesford will continue designing its LCTS scheme for Uttlesford residents after the Government withdrew the Essex LGR decision
findings.detail: The paper says LCTS changes had been due to be modelled and consulted on in summer 2027 with Epping Forest and Harlow councils under Local Government Reform. Following the withdrawal of the Essex LGR decision, officers will continue designing a scheme for Uttlesford residents alone.
findings.matters: A planned joint scheme across three Essex councils has been dropped, so the council will carry the design and cost of its own scheme rather than sharing it.
findings.quote: Following the Government’s withdrawal of the Essex LGR decision, Uttlesford staff will continue to design and develop a scheme for Uttlesford residents only.

findings.headline: Uttlesford's contribution income is modelled with collection ranging from 87% to 90%.
findings.detail: The paper states the council's income figures are gross, and that actual income received will be lower because collection ranges from 87% to 90%. The £18,728 council share is calculated using an average award, which could rise or fall with caseload during the year.
findings.matters: Collection assumptions determine how much of the stated contribution income reaches the council, so a finance director can judge the gap between modelled and received income.
findings.figures: 87% to 90% income collection range; £18,728 council share of contribution income at 12.5%
findings.quote: Income collection ranges from 87% to 90% so the actual income received is likely to be lower than the figures

findings.headline: The major preceptors' share-back of income to Uttlesford is estimated at £61,131 for 2027/28, up from £40,000 in 2026/27.
findings.detail: The table sets out a major preceptors income share-back to UDC, which the paper says is based on the preceptor share back estimate on 2026/27 predicted collection rates. Preceptors have agreed to share their element of increased income generated from fraud and compliance activity.
findings.matters: Preceptor share-back offsets the council's scheme cost, and it depends on collection rates and fraud work, so a finance director can see how much of the net cost it is expected to cover.
findings.figures: £61,131 major preceptors income share-back 2027/28 (UDC column); £40,000 major preceptors income share-back 2026/27 (UDC column)
findings.quote: the preceptor share back estimate on 2026/27 predicted collection rates

findings.headline: Total LCTS claimants fell for a fourth year to 3,131 at 1 April 2026, while disabled claimants rose to 1,299, up 63
findings.detail: The paper reports a fourth year of falling total claimants, with the largest fall in the working age category. It notes that the fall is offset by a further rise in vulnerable and disabled claimants, which has risen each year for five years.
findings.matters: A shift in caseload towards the 0% contribution group reduces the council's income from contributions while total numbers fall, which affects the scheme's cost mix.
findings.figures: 3,131 total claimants at 1/4/26; 3,325 total claimants at 1/4/22; 1,299 vulnerable/disabled claimants at 1/4/26, up 63 in year
findings.quote: The overall number of claimants has reduced for the fourth year in a row

findings.headline: Uttlesford's estimated 2027/28 net cost of its LCTS scheme is £663,543, against £594,630 in 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper gives the forecast UDC position for 2027/28 based on caseload expenditure at 1 April 2026 and predicted collection rates. The LCTS discounts line for the council's share rises from £612,630 to £636,843 in the table.
findings.matters: The council's own share of scheme cost is rising in a year when the paper also reports falling total caseload, so the cost increase is not explained by caseload volume alone.
findings.figures: £663,543 estimated UDC net cost 2027/28; £594,630 UDC total net cost 2026/27; £636,843 UDC share of LCTS discounts 2027/28; £612,630 UDC share of LCTS discounts 2026/27
findings.quote: the forecast financial position for UDC in 2027/28 will be an estimated net cost of £663,543.

daily_post.headline: KPMG notes the Constitution is dated September 2023 with no expected review date, and recommends a version number and review date on policies.
daily_post.lead: A governance recommendation on policy review dates is a routine-looking item that other councils' audit committees may be asked to check in their own documents.
